kunyah: Umm al-Mu'minin — Mother of the Believers
tribe: Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza, Quraysh
teaser: The first human being to believe. She held him while he trembled and said Allah would never disgrace him.
quran_mention: Her title comes from the ayah on the wives of the Prophet ﷺ: «وَأَزْوَاجُهُ أُمَّهَاتُهُمْ» — 'and his wives are their mothers.' (33:6)

layers.title: Who She Was
layers.subtitle: She hired him before anyone else believed him
layers.content:
Khadijah bint Khuwaylid ibn Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza ibn Qusayy — Quraysh on both sides, of the clan of Banu Asad.

Ibn Ishaq describes a businesswoman of standing and wealth in a city that lived by trade. She did not travel the routes herself. She engaged men to run her caravans and paid them a share of the profit, which means she was assessing character for a living. Prominent men of Makkah had asked to marry her. She had turned them all down.

What reached her about the young Muhammad was not his lineage, which she already knew, but three specific things: that his word held, that he was scrupulously honest, and that he was gentle with people. So she sent for him and offered him a caravan to Syria at a better rate than she paid anyone else, and sent her servant Maysarah along with him.

Maysarah came home with a report, and the ledger came home better than usual. She was forty. He was twenty-five. She sent her friend Nafisah bint Munyah to sound him out; he agreed and asked his uncles to speak to hers. Banu Hashim and the chiefs of Mudar witnessed the contract. He gave twenty camels as her dowry, and married no one else for as long as she lived.
layers.source: Ibn Ishaq, via al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar; Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III

layers.title: The Conversion
layers.subtitle: Cover me, he said — and she did more than that
layers.content:
Aisha narrated what happened, and it is preserved in Sahih al-Bukhari at the very opening of the book. The seclusion in the cave of Hira. The angel. 'Recite.' 'I cannot recite.' Three times, until the words came: «اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ» — 'Read, in the name of your Lord who created.'

He came down the mountain shaking and reached his house and said, 'Cover me, cover me.' They covered him until the trembling passed. Then he told her what had happened in the cave, and that he was afraid.

Her answer is the first act of faith in Islam, and notice that it is not a theological argument. It is an inventory of his life. 'Allah will never disgrace you. You unite the ties of kinship. You bear the burden of the weak. You help the poor and the needy. You entertain the guest. You endure hardship for the sake of the truth.' She had watched him for fifteen years and she told him what she had seen.

Then she took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, an old blind man who read the earlier scriptures, and said: 'My cousin, listen to your nephew.' Ibn Sa'd records that his teachers agreed on one point without dispute — the first of the people of the qibla to respond to the Messenger of Allah was Khadijah bint Khuwaylid.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 96:1-3 — 'Read, in the name of your Lord who created; created man from a clinging form. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous'
layers.hadith_ref: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Beginning of Revelation — narrated by Aisha
layers.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, narrated by Aisha, via al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar; Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III

layers.title: With the Prophet ﷺ
layers.subtitle: Twenty-five years, and a greeting sent down for her
layers.content:
Their marriage lasted about twenty-five years and he took no other wife in all of it. Every one of his children except Ibrahim was hers: al-Qasim, Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, Fatimah, and Abdullah. The house in Makkah before the Hijrah was the two of them and those children.

She was not a bystander to the mission. She was its first funder, its first defender, and for a while the only person on earth who took his side. That is the plain meaning of what he said about her later: she helped and comforted him with herself and with her wealth when the people would not.

And there is a moment recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari, narrated by Abu Hurayrah, that is unlike anything else in the seerah. Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and said that Khadijah was on her way to him carrying a vessel of food or drink; that when she arrived he should convey to her the greeting of peace from her Lord; and that he should give her the good news of a house of jewels in the Garden, with no noise in it and no weariness.

She was in her sixties, walking across Makkah with a bowl of food for her husband. The message came down ahead of her.
layers.hadith_ref: Sahih al-Bukhari — narrated by Abu Hurayrah: Jibril conveyed to Khadijah the greeting of her Lord and the tidings of a house in the Garden with no noise and no toil
layers.source: Sahih al-Bukhari; al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: The richest woman in Makkah, hungry in a valley
layers.content:
Quraysh eventually stopped arguing and moved to starvation. Banu Hashim and those with them were confined in a valley outside Makkah and cut off from trade and marriage. al-Mubarakpuri records that the crying of children from hunger could be heard from there, and that food only got in when a few Makkans smuggled it, or during the sacred months when hostilities paused and the confined could buy — at prices set to be out of reach.

One of the smugglers was her own nephew, Hakim ibn Hizam, carrying wheat to his aunt Khadijah. Abu Jahl intercepted him on the road and tried to stop him. He only got through because another Qurayshi, al-Bukhtari, intervened.

Hold the two facts together. She had been one of the wealthiest people in that city and had turned down its most eligible men. Now her nephew had to smuggle her flour past a man who had grown up in her neighbourhood.

She had also buried sons. al-Qasim and Abdullah both died as small children. There is no narration of her wavering in any of it, and no narration of her asking her husband to make the boycott stop. Her wealth had already gone into the mission it was punishing.
layers.source: al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — the boycott of Banu Hashim; Ibn Hisham

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: The year he named after losing her
layers.content:
She died in Ramadan of the tenth year of the mission, two or three months after Abu Talib. Reports on her age place her at about sixty-five; the Prophet ﷺ was around fifty. He called that year the Year of Grief, and the name stuck to it permanently. Within months of losing her, sand was thrown on his head in the street and he went to Ta'if and was driven out of there too.

Years later, when someone raised the subject of her, he answered with four clauses, and they are the most complete testimony any companion received from him. She believed in me when the people disbelieved me. She trusted me when the people called me a liar. She helped and comforted me, with herself and with her wealth, when the people would not. And Allah gave me children by her.

What the ummah kept from Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, is not an office or a battle or a chapter of law. It is a template for what belief looks like at the very start, before there is a community, a mosque, a name for the religion, or any evidence that it will survive. It looks like one person listening carefully to another and saying: I know who you are, and Allah will not disgrace you.
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'She believed in me while the people disbelieved me; she trusted me while the people belied me; she helped and comforted me in person and wealth when the people would not' — Musnad Ahmad, cited by al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

quiz.prompt: How did Khadijah and the Prophet ﷺ first come into contact?

options.text: Abu Talib arranged a marriage between the families
She hired him to run a trading caravan to Syria
They were neighbours in the same quarter of Makkah
He came to her seeking a loan

quiz.citation: Ibn Ishaq, via al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: She engaged men to run her caravans for a share of the profit, and offered him a better rate than she paid anyone else. What she had heard about him was his truthfulness, his honesty and his manners.

quiz.prompt: What did Khadijah say when the Prophet ﷺ came home from the cave frightened?

options.text: 'Wait until Waraqah has judged the matter'
'This has happened to prophets before you'
'Allah will never disgrace you' — then listed the good he did with his life
'Tell no one until you are certain'

quiz.citation: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Beginning of Revelation — narrated by Aisha
quiz.scholar_reflection: She named the specifics: he kept kinship ties, carried the weak, helped the poor, hosted the guest, bore hardship for truth. Her faith began as careful observation of a person over fifteen years.

quiz.prompt: What did Jibril tell the Prophet ﷺ to convey to Khadijah as she approached carrying food?

options.text: That her wealth had been accepted as charity
The greeting of peace from her Lord, and tidings of a house in the Garden with no noise and no toil
That she would live to see Makkah conquered
That her children would all enter Paradise

quiz.citation: Sahih al-Bukhari — narrated by Abu Hurayrah
quiz.scholar_reflection: She was walking across Makkah with a bowl in her hands. The greeting was sent down to meet her on the way.

quiz.prompt: During the boycott of Banu Hashim, who smuggled wheat to Khadijah?

options.text: Her nephew Hakim ibn Hizam
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq
Her servant Maysarah
Waraqah ibn Nawfal

quiz.citation: al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — the confinement of Banu Hashim
quiz.scholar_reflection: Abu Jahl intercepted him on the road and tried to stop the delivery. He got through only because al-Bukhtari stepped in. The wealthiest woman in Makkah was being fed in secret.

quiz.prompt: What did the Prophet ﷺ name the year in which Khadijah and Abu Talib both died?

options.text: The Year of the Elephant
The Year of Ashes
The Year of Grief
The Year of the Delegation

quiz.citation: al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — the tenth year of prophethood
quiz.scholar_reflection: The name stuck permanently. He also said afterwards that Quraysh never affected him the way they did once Abu Talib was gone — the loss of protection and the loss of his wife arrived together.

quiz.prompt: Khadijah's belief started as fifteen years of watching how one man treated people. What do you actually use to decide whether to trust someone?

options.text: Their track record over time, nothing faster
How they treat people who cannot help them
My instinct in the first few minutes
What people I already trust say about them

quiz.citation: Reflection on Aisha's narration of the first revelation, Sahih al-Bukhari
quiz.scholar_reflection: She had already made a living out of judging men's character before hiring them. When the hardest claim in history was put to her, she checked it against the man.

quiz.prompt: He came home frightened and asked to be covered. She listened before she reassured. What is your reflex when someone brings you something they cannot explain?

options.text: I reach for a solution almost immediately
I go quiet because I am afraid of saying the wrong thing
I listen, but I am already forming my verdict
I can sit with it without needing to resolve it

quiz.citation: Reflection on the narration of Aisha, Sahih al-Bukhari
quiz.scholar_reflection: She covered him first, waited for the trembling to pass, listened, reassured, and only then took him to someone with knowledge. The order of those four things is worth noticing.

quiz.prompt: She had turned down the most prominent men in Makkah, then ended up hungry in a valley for the sake of what she believed. What would that trade cost you?

options.text: More than I want to admit — I care how I am seen
The comfort, more than the standing
Not much, because I do not have much status to lose
I would do it, but I would want it to be recognised

quiz.citation: Reflection on the boycott of Banu Hashim, al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: No narration records her asking for the boycott to be ended, or reminding her husband what she had given up. That silence in the sources is itself a kind of testimony.

quiz.prompt: The Prophet ﷺ said she believed him when others called him a liar. Who has believed you when it was not obvious that they should?

options.text: One person, and I know exactly who
Several — I have been luckier than I admit
No one yet, and it has shaped me
I am more often the one doing the believing

quiz.citation: Musnad Ahmad, cited by al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: There is no substitute for the first person who takes you seriously. He was still naming it years after her death, in front of people who had come along later.

quiz.prompt: Her legacy is not an office or a battle but a way of standing beside someone. Where in your life could you be that for a person?

options.text: Someone specific comes to mind straight away
I support people but keep an exit open
I would want to know I was backing the right side first
I would rather be supported than be the support

quiz.citation: Reflection on the life of Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: She backed him when the outcome was completely unknown and the entire city was against it. Certainty came later, and it came partly because she had already committed.
